{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./nv_devicequery.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -c 4                 -> -c 4
#   -t 6:00:00           -> -t 6h
#   --gres=gpu:...:2     -> -g 2  (GPU model constraint not translated)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 2 -t 6h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p gpu not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the gpu partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm requested GPU model teslaK80 via --gres=gpu:teslaK80:2.
  # Flux portable request only expresses GPU count (-g 2); no model constraint is applied.
  # Performance implication: job may run on a different GPU type, changing performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o/-e used %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  module load gcc/6.2.0
  module load cuda/10.0

  echo "#---------"
  echo "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
  nvidia-smi
  nvidia-smi | grep "|\\    [$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES] |" | awk '{print $3}' | xargs -r ps -o pid,ppid,uid -p
  echo "#----------"

  flux run -n 1 -c 4 -g 2 ~/nvida_samples/1_Utilities/deviceQuery/deviceQuery
fi
"
}
